reason: Para 3 does assert the spirit/soul opposition and the quote is accurate, but the entire paragraph is Jung expounding Lambspringk's symbolism (the fishes 'symbolize the spirit/soul polarity', soul 'densior et crassior' than spirit is the alchemical doctrine), not an independent psychological assertion by Jung.
Para 3 states verbatim that the water the fishes swim in 'is mare nostrum (our sea) and is interpreted as the body'; claim_type jung-reports-parallel with Lambspringk source is correct.
Para 3 states 'The stag signifies the soul, the unicorn spirit, and the forest the body' within the Lambspringk material; quote, direction, and claim_type with source are all correct.
Same Lambspringk sentence in para 3 assigns the unicorn to spirit; quote exact, direction and claim_type correct.
Para 4 states in Jung's own voice that the pairs of opposites 'do not belong to the ego-personality but are supraordinate to it'; quote accurate, direction correct, jung-asserts appropriate.

Para 5, in Jung's own voice ('As I have shown elsewhere'), says 'the aim of the circulatio is the production (or rather, reproduction) of the Original Man, who was a sphere'; Original Man = Anthropos is standard usage in this chapter (cf. para 12).

Para 10 states 'The unifying agent is the spirit Mercurius' and describes 'Mercurius as a peacemaker, the mediator between the warring elements and producer of unity'; the elements in question are the four combined elements of the quaternio (para 5). Quote accurate.
Para 12 states in Jung's own voice 'Mercurius corresponds to the Holy Ghost as well as to the Anthropos'; quote exact, jung-asserts correct.
Same sentence in para 12 supports mercurius corresponds-to anthropos; quote exact, direction and claim_type correct.

Para 12 states that 'the mandala, which we find so often in the drawings of our patients, corresponds to the vessel of transformation' (circle = Hermetic vessel); quote accurate, jung-asserts correct.
Para 14 states 'Above all, the prima materia is the mother of the lapis, the filius philosophorum'; quote exact, direction correct, jung-asserts appropriate.
Para 14: 'Isis, however, is also the healer... As such she personifies that arcane substance, be it dew or the aqua permanens'; the ellipsis bridges the Ra/Osiris healing material without distortion.

Para 16, in Jung's own evaluative voice, says 'Maier was fully justified in giving the name Isis to the prima materia or feminine transformative substance', i.e. Isis amplifies the prima materia concept; quote exact.

Para 19 does state 'The identification of Malchuth with Luna forms a link with alchemy', but the identification is made in the quoted Vigenerus/Zohar material ('[The Sefiroth] end in Malchuth or the moon') and Jung reports it as a Cabalistic-alchemical assimilation, not as his own assertion.

reason: Para 19 says Luna 'is duplex and mutable like Mercurius, and is like him a mediator; hence their identification in alchemy' — the identification is attributed to alchemy (with a source footnote), so this is a reported alchemical identification, not Jung's own assertion.

Para 21 explicitly quotes the 'Consilium coniugii': 'So also the moisture of the moon, when she receives his light, slays the sun, and at the birth of the child of the Philosophers she dies likewise'; the ellipsis omits only 'when she receives his light' without distortion, and jung-quotes-source with Consilium coniugii is correct.

Para 27's sentence 'The conjunction of the moist (= moon) and the hot (= sun) thus produces the balsam' is Jung's summary of Dorn's doctrine in 'De tenebris contra naturam' (the balsamum vitae as 'a true mixture of the natural heat with its radical moisture'), so it is reported alchemical doctrine rather than Jung's own assertion.

Para 29 states 'the changefulness of the moon is paralleled by the transformation of the pre-existent Christ... through the "emptying"', but the parallel rests on the Philippians 2:6 kenosis passage and patristic commentary (Hilary, Ephraem Syrus) that Jung is reporting as a theological analogy, not a plain Jungian assertion.
